Randomly downsample a 10x fragment file

Source: R/downsample.R
downsample_fragments.Rd

Stream a coordinate-sorted, bgzipped fragment file once and keep each fragment record independently with probability keep_prob (SplitMix64 RNG seeded with seed; header lines starting with # are always kept), then write BGZF output and build a tabix BED index. This is an R wrapper around the packaged shell script system.file("scripts", "downsample_fragments_fast.sh", package = "scRTtools"), which compiles a small C sampler with cc at run time.

Usage

downsample_fragments(
  input,
  output,
  keep_prob,
  seed = 20260821,
  threads = 16L,
  compression_level = 1L,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  bgzip = Sys.which("bgzip"),
  tabix = Sys.which("tabix"),
  cc = Sys.which("cc"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

input

Path to the input .tsv.gz fragment file.

output

Path to the output .tsv.gz file (must differ from input; its directory must exist and be writable).

keep_prob

Keep probability in (0, 1], e.g. optimize_shrink_factor()$shrink_factor.

seed

Non-negative integer seed of the sampler.

threads

Positive integer; bgzip threads.

compression_level

Integer 0-9; bgzip compression level.

overwrite

Logical; replace an existing output and index.

bgzip, tabix, cc

Paths to the bgzip, tabix and C compiler executables. Default: found on PATH.

verbose

Logical; show the script's progress output. Default FALSE.

Value

Invisibly, output.

Details

Besides output, the script writes <output>.tbi and <output>.downsample_info.txt (parameters and kept/total record counts). Results are reproducible for a given seed and input.
